T7.description: Bacteriophage T7 RNA polymerase promoter. Strongest bacterial promoter; requires T7 RNAP (e.g. BL21(DE3) strain). Inducible by IPTG.

trc.description: Hybrid trp/lac promoter. Strong constitutive/IPTG-inducible. Requires lacI repressor.

lac.description: Classic lac operon promoter. IPTG-inducible, weak without lacUV5 mutation.

araBAD.description: Arabinose-inducible promoter. Tightly regulated; repressed by glucose.

GAL1.description: Galactose-inducible promoter from the GAL1 gene. Very strong inducible promoter; repressed by glucose, induced by galactose.
GAL1.notes: Gold standard for inducible overexpression in S. cerevisiae; used in pYES2.

TEF1.description: Translation Elongation Factor 1-alpha promoter. Strong constitutive promoter; active in all growth conditions.
TEF1.notes: Most commonly used strong constitutive promoter; ~700 bp.

TDH3.description: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase promoter (also called GPD). Very strong constitutive; one of the strongest in yeast.
TDH3.notes: Strongest constitutive promoter in yeast; may cause metabolic burden at high copy number.

ADH1.description: Alcohol dehydrogenase 1 promoter. Medium-strength constitutive; well-characterized.

CYC1.description: Cytochrome c isoform 1 promoter. Weak constitutive; useful for low-level expression.
CYC1.notes: Weak basal expression; often used as minimal promoter in regulatory studies.

GAL10.description: Galactose-inducible promoter from the GAL10 gene. Strong inducible; divergent from GAL1 on chromosome II. Used as the second promoter in pESC dual-expression vectors.
GAL10.notes: Shares a bi-directional regulatory region with GAL1; co-induced by galactose. In pESC vectors GAL1 and GAL10 drive two independent MCS in opposite orientations.

CUP1.description: Copper-metallothionein promoter. Tightly regulated; repressed at baseline, induced by copper sulfate (0.1–0.5 mM CuSO4).
CUP1.notes: Useful when galactose-based induction is impractical (e.g. metabolic studies). Dose-dependent response from ~0.05–0.5 mM CuSO4. Avoid in copper-sensitive assays.

MET25.description: Methionine-repressible promoter. Strong in methionine-free media; repressed by adding methionine (1–5 mM). Useful for conditional knockdown or titratable expression.
MET25.notes: Active in SC-MET (methionine drop-out); shut off by adding methionine to media. An alternative to GAL1 when carbon source must remain glucose.

CaMV35S.description: Cauliflower Mosaic Virus 35S promoter. Constitutive, high expression in most dicots. Weak in monocots.
CaMV35S.sequence_note: Full-length 35S is ~946 bp; double 35S (d35S) gives 2x expression

FMV35S.description: Figwort Mosaic Virus 35S promoter. Constitutive; better monocot expression than CaMV35S.

Ubi1.description: Maize Ubiquitin-1 promoter. Strong constitutive expression in monocots (maize, wheat, rice). Preferred for biolistics.
Ubi1.notes: Often paired with Ubi1 intron for enhanced expression

NOS.description: Nopaline synthase promoter from A. tumefaciens. Weak constitutive expression in plants; mainly used for selectable markers.
